Trail: fix(sem): seven wrong-answer defects in the provider and type scanners
  Number:  157
  ID:      01M1NERAE17SC5D95758TTSGCP
  Branch:  fix/provider-and-types-findings
  Base:    main
  Status:  open
  Author:  suhaanthayyil
  Phase:   building
  URL:     https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/157
  Assignees: suhaanthayyil
  Type:      task
  Created: 2026-09-04T05:37:37Z
  Updated: 2026-09-05T16:09:20Z

Description:
Problem:
The semantic provider and type scanners contained seven wrong-answer defects:
Completeness assurance gap — repositories with >25% of tracked files never parsed (due to size limits) reported "ok" instead of "degraded", silencing correctness gates.
GraphQL operation parsing — parameters with nested braces ($f: Filter = {enabled: true}) were rejected, losing entire operations.
GraphQL tag detection — template literal tags separated from backticks by whitespace were not recognized, losing shorthand operations.
GraphQL field name contamination — template interpolations (${expr}) produced invalid field names ($, n) in the graph.
Go interface call binding — methods with mismatched signatures (e.g., Run(string) error vs. Run() error) were treated as valid implementations, producing wrong CALLS edges.
Go qualified receiver routing — receivers like foo.Communicator resolved by directory basename instead of import path, picking decoy same-named packages over the actual import.
Ignore policy explosion — one unreadable nested .gitignore failed the entire repository walk; now excludes only that subtree with a warning.
Vendor negation scope — a single !package/ in vendor/.gitignore re-admitted the whole vendored tree instead of just that package.
Ambiguous registration aliases — command handler names appearing in multiple packages/languages attached the alias to all of them; now attach only when unambiguous.
Solution:
Added hardened parsers and relation builders:
Completeness level now checks parsed-file ratio ≥75% and degrades below that threshold, catching silently degraded corpora.
GraphQL parameter regex widened to allow nested braces; tag detection scans backward through whitespace; root field scanner rejects $-prefixed and backslash-escaped names.
Go interface implementation checker validates parameter and result type signatures match before accepting a method as satisfying an interface requirement.
Go qualified receiver resolver consults the file's import table to bind qualifiers to import paths, with basename fallback only when imports are unavailable.
Filesystem walk fallback excludes subtrees whose .gitignore is unreadable (size or permission) and reports the omission as W_WALK_UNREADABLE_IGNORE_POLICY; operation-wide rule allowance errors still abort.
Vendored path verdict now checks ReincludesPath for each path individually instead of ReincludesDescendant on its ancestor.
Registration alias attachment deferred to after parsing the full corpus; aliases attach only to symbols with unique short names.
No public API change. Schema contract stable; SCIP IDs unchanged.

Make an authenticated HTTP request to an Entire API and print the JSON response.

These endpoints are internal and can change shape without notice; where a
purpose-built command exists, its output is the stable interface.

The CLI attaches the right bearer token and dials the right host for the
chosen backend, so you don't have to plumb auth yourself:

  --to core   the control plane (default): orgs, repos, mirrors, clusters, /me
  --to cell   your home entire-api cell: /me/* activity, repo aggregates

Use --jurisdiction <slug> (e.g. us, eu) to reach a specific jurisdiction's
entire-api cell instead of your home one; it implies --to cell.

<path> is the full path on that host, e.g. /api/v1/clusters. These
placeholders are filled from the current repo's origin remote:
  {owner} {repo}   the GitHub owner / repo
  {repo_id}        the repo's Entire ULID (from its mirror) — cells key on this

The method is GET unless a field/body is given (then POST); override with -X.

When to use this:
LAST RESORT. Right in two cases: you are developing against Entire's own
APIs and want a raw response, or no first-class command covers your need.
Otherwise prefer the command built for the job (checkpoint, session, trail,
status, repo, …) — its output is stable, raw endpoints are not. If you are
reaching for this during ordinary work in a repo with Entire enabled, run
`entire agent-help` first; there is probably a command for it. When you do
need it, use this rather than hand-rolling curl — it attaches the right
bearer and dials the right host for you.

  entire api --to cell /api/v1/me/activity
  entire api --jurisdiction eu /api/v1/me/activity

      "textSnapshot": "Problem:\nThe semantic provider and type scanners contained seven wrong-answer defects:\nCompleteness assurance gap — repositories with \u003e25% of tracked files never parsed (due to size limits) reported \"ok\" instead of \"degraded\", silencing correctness gates.\nGraphQL operation parsing — parameters with nested braces ($f: Filter = {enabled: true}) were rejected, losing entire operations.\nGraphQL tag detection — template literal tags separated from backticks by whitespace were not recognized, losing shorthand operations.\nGraphQL field name contamination — template interpolations (${expr}) produced invalid field names ($, n) in the graph.\nGo interface call binding — methods with mismatched signatures (e.g., Run(string) error vs. Run() error) were treated as valid implementations, producing wrong CALLS edges.\nGo qualified receiver routing — receivers like foo.Communicator resolved by directory basename instead of import path, picking decoy same-named packages over the actual import.\nIgnore policy explosion — one unreadable nested .gitignore failed the entire repository walk; now attach only when unambiguous.\nSolution:\nAdded hardened parsers and relation builders:\nCompleteness level now checks parsed-file ratio ≥75% and degrades below that threshold, catching silently degraded corpora.\nGraphQL parameter regex widened to allow nested braces; tag detection scans backward through whitespace; root field scanner rejects $-prefixed and backslash-escaped names.\nGo interface implementation checker validates parameter and result type signatures match before accepting a method as satisfying an interface requirement.\nGo qualified receiver resolver consults the file's import table to bind qualifiers to import paths, with basename fallback only when imports are unavailable.\nFilesystem walk fallback excludes subtrees whose .gitignore is unreadable (size or permission) and reports the omission as W_WALK_UNREADABLE_IGNORE_POLICY; operation-wide rule allowance errors still abort.\nVendored path verdict now checks ReincludesPath for each path individually instead of ReincludesDescendant on its ancestor.\nRegistration alias attachment deferred to after parsing the full corpus; aliases attach only to symbols with unique short names.\nNo public API change. tag detection scans backward through whitespace; root field scanner rejects $-prefixed and backslash-escaped names.\nGo interface implementation checker validates parameter and result type signatures match before accepting a method as satisfying an interface requirement.\nGo qualified receiver resolver consults the file's import table to bind qualifiers to import paths, with basename fallback only when imports are unavailable.\nFilesystem walk fallback excludes subtrees whose .gitignore is unreadable (size or permission) and reports the omission as W_WALK_UNREADABLE_IGNORE_POLICY; operation-wide rule allowance errors still abort.\nVendored path verdict now checks ReincludesPath for each path individually instead of ReincludesDescendant on its ancestor.\nRegistration alias attachment deferred to after parsing the full corpus; aliases attach only to symbols with unique short names.\nNo public API change. - Lazy import-loading performance.

**Two remain open: one medium, one low.**

- Add fixtures where handler names appear only in comments or ordinary strings. Measure parser invocations and benchmark the extra work.
- Make the prefilter syntax-aware for languages where comments and strings can safely be excluded. Preserve embedded-code regions and use conservative fallback for unsupported syntax.
- Verify identical symbols, aliases, ambiguity decisions, and stream ordering before and after the change.
- Resolve once unnecessary parsing decreases without losing real handler candidates.

- Distinguish **matching**, **different**, and **unknown** type identities. Emit an implementation hop only when matching is established.
- Preserve correct matches for import aliases, built-in aliases, and same-package types. Test unresolved imports and ambiguous cases explicitly.
- Resolve after the false edge disappears and the existing valid-match tests pass.

Then run the relevant tests, full checks, and fresh trail evaluations. These changes are planned, not implemented.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)
